overall: AUDIT PASSED with minor corrections. (a) Code review of /home/user/multi-agent-environment/frontier/order_ensemble.py: no correctness bugs found. Prefix products correctly include A (t_j = A*Q_j mod q, built incrementally); no off-by-one (prefixes start at Q_1 = ell_{sigma(1)}, consistent with the spec's j=1..K); phase is exp(2*pi*i*(a*t mod q)/q), correct; Miller-Rabin base set (2..37) is deterministic far beyond q <= 2e8; random_prime_in's |1 bump is guarded by c <= hi; mid-rank percentile via bisect is correct; ks_uniform implements the exact one-sample KS D; z_of_meanV = (mean V_order - rand mean)/(rand sd/sqrt(40)) is a standard and honest effect size; the shared sequential RNG makes the whole run deterministic. Re-running the script reproduces the stored JSON EXACTLY (all data fields identical; only runtime_seconds fields differ), and the surprising 8 s total runtime is real (7.3 s measured). All 12 table rows, all pooled statistics (inc mean pct 0.5196, z 1.49, KS 0.0458, tails 26/35; dec 0.5193/1.46/0.0500/30/35; adv_mult 0.5204/1.55/0.0483/17/17), per-X pooled numbers, KS critical values (0.2147/0.1240/0.0620), K values (47/135/353/1033 = pi(2X)-pi(X)), and adv_spec==inc for 160/160 moduli were independently recomputed from the raw JSON and match verbatim. (b) Independent reimplementation (my own code: sympy primality, cmath, exact big-integer products with single reduction, different seed; X=300, 10 moduli, 50 random orders, a=1) reaches the same conclusions: rand mean 1.034, sd 1.103 (Exp(1) null), inc percentiles uniform-looking (mean 0.550, KS 0.200 vs crit 0.429); and it reproduces the agent's stored V_inc values for q=170263 to all six printed digits (0.093801, 0.521737, 0.271346), independently validating their walk computation. The G = K(V-1) identity was verified both algebraically (trivial: |sum|^2 = K + sum_{i!=k}) and numerically (G = 59.129575 = K(V-1), imag ~1e-14). (c) Statistics: the percentile-uniformity design is sound (mid-rank handles the discrete 1/400 grid; KS vs continuous uniform is slightly conservative for discrete support, which only strengthens a pass); the correlation caveat (harmonics share the walk and ensemble, effective n ~160, deflate z by ~sqrt(3)) is correctly reasoned, and the shared-ensemble explanation for the co-moving mild positive lean of inc/dec/adv_mult is legitimate since all three are ranked against the SAME 200-order ensemble per q. Effect sizes are reported honestly overall. CORRECTIONS (non-fatal): (1) the summary line 'mean 1.00 +/- 0.01, sd 0.98-1.02 in every cell' is numerically wrong — actual ranges are rand mean 0.986-1.023 and rand sd 0.951-1.019 (the agent's own table shows 0.951 and 1.023, so this is an internal inconsistency/overstatement of precision; with se ~ 0.011 per cell mean the data remain fully Exp(1)-consistent, so the substance stands); (2) 'regenerates the JSON byte-comparably up to float formatting' should say 'up to the runtime_seconds fields' — data fields are bit-identical; (3) claim 6's status 'provable-sketch' is generous — it is an interpretation/diagnostic with no proof sketch; better labelled 'interpretation/unverified extrapolation', as the writeup's own Limits section in fact concedes. Design deviations 1 (adv_spec ≡ inc since ell < 2X <= X^2 <= q, trivially true and machine-confirmed) and 2 (skipping G via the exact identity) are both correct and were properly flagged. Stop-rule: respected — an empirical exchangeability test of the order ensemble is not a reformulation of the archived additive kernel. Scope limits (single-modulus V, not shell-aggregated E_a or pair-sum kernel; finite panel cannot certify X^{o(1)}) are correctly stated. Bottom line: the experiment, its data, and its headline conclusion (increasing order statistically exchangeable with random orders; walk Steinhaus-generic at the critical length) are verified; only the three cosmetic misstatements above need fixing.

verdicts.claim: The specified adversarial order (sort by ell mod q) is identically the increasing order because q >= X^2 > 2X > ell.
verdicts.reason: Trivial: block primes satisfy ell < 2X <= X^2 <= q, so ell mod q = ell and the sort is the increasing order. Machine-confirmed adv_spec_equals_inc true for all 160 per-q rows in the JSON. Correctly flagged as a spec anomaly and sensibly replaced by the genuinely q-dependent adv_mult.

verdicts.claim: The q-dependent adversary adv_mult (sort by A*ell mod q) shows no elevation of V and is equally generic.
verdicts.reason: Recomputed pooled adv_mult statistics from raw data: mean pct 0.5204, KS 0.0483 < 0.0620, tails 17/17 vs expected 24, all per-cell KS <= 0.200 < 0.215; z_of_meanV range across all cells -1.64 to +2.20 with mixed signs. Numerically solid for this one adversary class; the note that multi-step/greedy adversaries were not tested is an honest and important scope limit — 'no simple residue-sorting adversary helps' should not be read as 'no adversary helps'.

verdicts.claim: G(sigma,q,a) is an exact linear function of V at a single modulus: sum_{i!=k} e_q(aA(Q_i-Q_k)) = |sum_j e_q(aAQ_j)|^2 - K, so G/K = V - 1.

Skipping G was legitimate; the caveat that the shell-aggregated weighted energy is a different object is correct and important.

verdicts.claim: No finite-size derandomization obstruction for vector B2: the true order carries no anomaly a random-order model theorem would miss; order-genericity offers no exploitable leverage.
